Documentation → Administration → App sign-in

Apps for people outside the console (App sign-in)

Give a Plugin Studio app to people who are not SATOM operators — they sign in on the app's own page, against the directory servers and groups you choose for that app, and reach that app and nothing else.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WherePlugin Studio → Apps → app → Sign-in tab · Plugin Studio → Sign-in directories (URL /studio/?pane=directories) · Access → Directory connections (URL /access/directory-connections/) · Access → App sign-in (URL /access/app-signin/) · Profiles → Type: Apps only · the people's portal at /a/

What is it?#

A way to hand one Plugin Studio app to a group of people who should not see the SATOM console: a help desk that looks something up, a team that raises a change. They sign in on the app's own page and land in a small portal (My apps) with the apps given to them — nothing else answers them. Each app can prove its people against its own directory servers and groups, different from the console's sign-in.

What does it do?#

  • Profiles → Type: Apps only. Such a profile holds no permission. Its accounts see My apps (/a/), their apps and an Account page. Their only menu is Plugins with those apps, every menu group already open; every console page answers not found, and the API v1 refuses their tokens (owner_forbidden).
  • Plugin Studio → Sign-in directories (also Access → Directory connections, the same list). Any number of Active Directory, LDAP and RADIUS / FortiAuthenticator servers, each with its own address, bind account and secret. They are independent of Settings → Authentication, which they never change.
  • Plugin Studio → Apps → app → Sign-in (also Access → App sign-in; a script app has the tab in its script editor). Per app: its own sign-in page and ordered rules — AD / LDAP group DNs and an optional LDAP filter, RADIUS groups, or local accounts — each optionally requiring a SATOM authenticator code.
  • The app package. The sign-in travels in app.json ("signin") and arrives switched off on import; the SATOM Builder edits it in its own Sign-in tab.
  1. 1Person opens /a/<app>/the app's sign-in page, in the app's colours
  2. 2Rules tried in orderfirst that accepts wins; never the console sign-in
  3. 3Account user@connectioncreated at the first sign-in, Apps only profile
  4. 4Second factor (if the rule asks)set up at the first sign-in
  5. 5The appand only the apps their sign-ins proved

Requirements#

  • A published (or, for a script app, published script) Plugin Studio app.
  • At least one profile with Type: Apps only (Access → Profiles → New Profile).
  • For directory rules: a directory connection that answers Test. For AD group checks the connection needs its Base DN.

Permissions#

Changing a sign-in or a directory connection needs users.manage, like Users and Groups: they decide who gets in — in Plugin Studio as on the Access pages (the same routes). A Plugin Studio author without it sees the app's Sign-in tab read only and no Sign-in directories pane; the Access URLs answer 403. Plugin Studio authors keep opening every app from the console.

How to use#

Create the Apps only profile#

  1. Access → Profiles → New Profile, Type: Apps only, a name such as Help desk apps. There is no permission to tick.

Add a directory connection#

  1. Plugin Studio → Sign-in directories → New connection (or Access → Directory connections).
  2. Pick the Kind, give an Id (fixed once saved — accounts are named user@<id>), the Host, and for AD the Base DN and AD domain; for LDAP the Bind DN, its password and the User filter; for RADIUS the Shared secret and NAS identifier.
  3. Save, then Test: without a user it checks the server answers; with a user and password it signs that user in (nothing is stored) and, for RADIUS, lists the groups the reply names.

Open an app to a group#

  1. Plugin Studio → Apps → the app → Sign-in tab (a script app: its script editor's Sign-in tab; or Access → App sign-in → the app).
  2. Tick People sign in to this app on its own page.
  3. Add rule for each connection, in the order to try them: - AD / LDAP: one group DN per line (member of any; AD counts nested groups) and, if needed, an LDAP filter such as (department=NOC). - RADIUS: the group names the FortiAuthenticator sends. - Tick Require a SATOM authenticator code where a second factor is wanted.
  4. Choose the Profile of the accounts a sign-in creates (only Apps only profiles are offered) and, if new people should wait, New accounts wait for an administrator.
  5. Save and hand out the link shown at the top: https://<node>/a/<app>/.

Give an app to accounts that already exist#

Tick groups or people under Shared with. They use it with the account they have — a console user from the console, an Apps only account from My apps.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Rule → group DNs AD / LDAP: the user must be a member of any of them No CN=helpdesk,OU=Groups,DC=corp,DC=local
Rule → LDAP filter ANDed with the user lookup No (department=NOC)
Rule → RADIUS groups Fortinet-Group-Name values, case-insensitive No satom-helpdesk
Rule → Require a SATOM authenticator code TOTP before the session starts No on
Profile of the accounts a sign-in creates an Apps only profile Yes, with a directory rule Help desk apps
New accounts wait for an administrator first sign-in lands disabled until enabled in Users No off

Move an app with its sign-in#

Export package (Plugin Studio → app → Publish) writes the rules into app.json as "signin": each directory connection by Id and kind, the groups, the filter, the authenticator tick, the Apps only profile by name and New accounts wait. Never a server, a bind account, a secret, nor whether the sign-in was on.

On Import app package the sign-in arrives switched off:

  • a rule whose connection this server does not have (or has with another kind) is left out, with a warning and a to-do to create it in Sign-in directories;
  • a profile name this server does not have is left empty, with a warning;
  • an app that already has sign-in rules here keeps them.

Turn it on in the app's Sign-in tab once the app is published. In the SATOM Builder the Sign-in tab offers the directory connections and Apps only profiles of the target SATOM and checks the rules as you type.

Result#

  • The person's account is user@<connection id>, with the chosen profile. It signs in only through that connection, on an app page: the console sign-in treats it as unknown, so a directory jdoe is never served the console's jdoe and two directories never share an account.
  • A sign-in proves its own app. A second app is a second sign-in, with that app's rules. The app's page lists who signed in, with Revoke.
  • Audit: login.app.ok, login.app.fail (which rule answered what — never a password), login.app.provision, login.app.2fa_enrol, app.signin.save, app.grant.revoke, directory_connection.*; a console page an Apps only account asked for leaves ACCESS_DENY reason=apps_only in the log.

Troubleshooting#

"Invalid username or password." although the password is right#

Possible causes - The user is not in any listed group (AD: check the DN; nested membership counts), or does not match the LDAP filter. - RADIUS: the Access-Accept names no Fortinet-Group-Name, or another group. The FortiAuthenticator sends a group's Fortinet-Group-Name only when the group carries it as a RADIUS attribute and is in the group filter of the realm that accepted the user (the authentication profile of SATOM's RADIUS policy). A member of a group outside that filter gets nothing for it. - A local rule, but the app is not shared with that account.

Solution 1. Directory connections → Test with that user: it says whether the directory accepts the password and, for RADIUS, which groups the reply names. 2. Audit log → login.app.fail shows, per connection, what it answered.

Verification — the next sign-in lands in the app.

"Sign-in for new users needs the primary node."#

The person signed in for the first time on the read-only standby, which cannot create the account. Sign in on the primary; afterwards the standby works too.

The app page says "not found" after signing in to another app#

Each app is its own sign-in. Open /a/<app>/ of the other app and sign in there.

Someone lost their authenticator#

Access → Users → Clear 2FA on their account. The next sign-in through a rule that requires it sets up a new one.

Advanced What is stored and enforced
  • profiles.kind (console / apps; anything else confines). An Apps only profile's permission set is empty whatever its column holds.
  • directory_connections holds the non-secret settings; the secret is an app_settings row (Fernet), or only a marker when the vault is the secret store and holds it (directory/<id>). Deleting a connection deletes the vault copy first; a vault that refuses leaves the connection in place. These are not Plugin Studio connections, so app and script code cannot read them.
  • studio_apps.login_json is the app's policy. Its rules travel in an app package as "signin" (connection ids, never a server or a secret) and arrive switched off. A stored policy that no longer validates closes the page instead of widening it.
  • studio_app_grants records "this account may use this app". An app account may use the app while this browser session signed in through it as that account and the grant stands, so Revoke is immediate.
  • The gate is deny by default: the apps and apps_portal blueprints plus a short list of endpoints (static, sign-out, the theme logo, a script app's run page). A test walks the whole URL map with an Apps only account.
  • RADIUS group names are read from Fortinet-Group-Name (vendor 12356, attribute 1). Measured on FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3: with the attribute on the group (User Groups → the group → RADIUS Attributes → Fortinet / Fortinet-Group-Name) and the group in the realm's Filter by group of the policy's authentication profile, the Accept carries it; the same group outside that filter sends nothing, even for a member.
